root_cause.text: The bq256xx charger driver incorrectly registers a devm-managed threaded IRQ handler before devm-managed power supply registration, causing the power supply handle to be freed before the IRQ handler is unregistered during device removal, leading to a use-after-free when the handler calls power_supply_changed() on the freed pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the call to `bq256xx_power_supply_init()` (which allocates/registers the `power_supply` handle) before `devm_request_threaded_irq()`. The commit message explicitly states: "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler (since `devm_` naturally deallocates in reverse allocation order). This ... leads to a race condition where an interrupt can fire just _after_ the `power_supply` handle has been freed."
